symptom: Pinned main legacy manual workflow echoes the complete generated request JSON in a run step. The owner-supplied request_reference permits path-like punctuation and is copied into requestReference without privacy token denial; consequently a path-like reference supplied by an operator could be printed in Actions logs. This is conditional source-level exposure, not evidence that any private path was entered or leaked.
lesson: A field-format allowlist and owner-only dispatch guard do not make a free-form reference safe for unredacted logging. Distinguish input acceptance, JSON projection, and Actions log output; a harmless path-shaped synthetic input can reveal the source-level route without observing any private data.
guardrail: Keep the legacy workflow and runner unmodified pending operations-owner review. For future approved remediation, replace full request echo with an allowlisted metadata summary or redact free-form fields before logging; independently constrain reference identifiers to non-path opaque tokens. Never log private paths, secrets or raw odds, dispatch the legacy workflow for diagnosis, or infer an actual leak from static reachability.
